items.stem: Choose the particle that marks the direct object: "パンを食べます" uses which particle before 食べます?

options.rationale: Correct: を marks the direct object of a transitive verb such as 食べる.
が marks the subject, not the direct object here.
に marks a destination or indirect object, not this direct object.
で marks a location of action or means, not the direct object.

items.explanation: Correct: を marks the direct object of a transitive verb such as 食べる.

items.stem: Which TWO strategies help select the correct vocabulary item in an N3 context question?

options.text: Reading the whole sentence for meaning before choosing
options.rationale: Correct: context determines which word fits.

options.text: Checking which word collocates naturally with the others
options.rationale: Correct: natural collocation guides the right choice.

options.text: Always choosing the word with the most strokes
options.rationale: Stroke count is irrelevant to meaning.

options.text: Picking the first option without reading
options.rationale: Not reading the context leads to errors.

options.text: Choosing by the English alphabetical order
options.rationale: Alphabetical order does not apply to Japanese vocabulary choice.

items.explanation: Correct: context determines which word fits.
